h1: The 6 Best Printers Under $200 That Won't Drain You on Ink, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 printers under $200, from ink tank models to office inkjets, scored on running cost, document feeding, duplex and footprint.
summary: The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the printer to buy under $200 if you print regularly, since its refillable ink keeps the cost per page low. HP's Smart Tank 5101 is the one with a long ink supply already in the box, the Epson ET-4800 adds a document feeder and fax, and the HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e gives you a feeder and duplex without an ink tank. The HP DeskJet 4355 is the cheapest way to get a printer in the door.
intro: The cheapest printers are often the most expensive to own. A sub-$100 inkjet ships with starter cartridges that run dry within weeks, and replacement cartridges can cost nearly as much as the printer. Anyone who prints more than a few pages a week should treat the sticker price as a down payment, and judge the machine by what the next two years of ink will cost.

This ranking sorts six printers that can be had under $200 by that logic. We reviewed each from its listing, comparing ink system, document feeder, duplex, connectivity and footprint. Where the listing mentions a limit, such as a 2.4GHz-only wireless radio, we call it out. A monochrome laser that sits just above the budget was left out, so every pick here fits the price promise.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Refillable ink bottles come in the box, and the cost per page stays low for years.
products.description:
Epson's ET-2800 uses the EcoTank refillable ink system, with bottled ink refills included, and prints, scans and copies wirelessly. It is built compactly for a home office and costs $100 to $200.

The case for it is long-run cost. Instead of buying small cartridges at a steep markup, you pour ink from bottles into onboard tanks, and one set of bottles lasts far longer than a cartridge pair. For a household or small office printing regularly, that arithmetic favors the tank system by a wide margin. It sits above the HP Smart Tank 5101 only because the listing has no wireless limitation and the brand's refill process is well established.

Buy it for steady printing at a lower cost per page. The caveat is that the first purchase is higher than a basic inkjet, and you give up a document feeder, so scanning stacks of paper is a manual job.
pros: Ink bottles included in the box
cons: Higher entry price than basic inkjets
products.idealFor: Households and small offices that print every week.
products.skipIf: You print fewer than a few pages a month.

products.name: HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless All-in-One Refillable Printer
products.verdict: A refillable tank printer that ships with two years of ink and a smaller footprint.
products.description:
What HP packs into the 5101 is a bottle-fed tank system, two years of starter ink, and a body slimmer than most rival tank machines. Wi-Fi is limited to the 2.4GHz band, there is no fax or feeder, and the price is $100 to $200.

Its big selling point is the ink in the box. Two years of supply, at normal home use, removes the main worry about running costs, and it means the purchase price covers a long runway. It ranks second because the listing flags 2.4GHz-only Wi-Fi, which can be awkward on routers that merge bands, and because it has no feeder.

Choose it if you want the economics of a tank printer with a small body. The 2.4GHz limitation is the caveat, so check your router settings before relying on wireless setup.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want years of ink included and a small footprint.
products.skipIf: Your router only offers a combined 5GHz network.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless All-in-One Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Tank economics plus an automatic document feeder, fax and Ethernet.
products.description:
The ET-4800 extends the EcoTank idea with an automatic document feeder, print, scan, copy and fax functions, and both Ethernet and wireless connectivity. It is aimed at home office workloads and sits in the $100 to $200 range.

It takes third place because the extras cost more and are not for everyone. The feeder is the key addition: it scans a multi-page contract or batch of receipts in one pass, which saves minutes on every job. Ethernet gives a stable connection when Wi-Fi is flaky. It ranks behind the HP Smart Tank 5101 only because that model includes two years of ink in its listing, while this one relies on standard refill bottles.

Pick it if you scan paper regularly or share the printer on a wired network. Skip it if you want the smallest ink-tank machine.
cons: Costs more than the base model
products.idealFor: Home offices that scan and file paperwork.
products.skipIf: You never scan more than a page or two.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A feeder and automatic duplex without paying for an ink-tank body.
products.description:
HP's OfficeJet Pro 8125e puts an automatic document feeder and automatic duplex printing into a color inkjet that falls in the $50 to $100 bucket. A 3-month Instant Ink trial and AI-enabled printing features come with it.

It is fourth because the hardware value is excellent but the ink model is not. You get office features at a low price, and in exchange you buy cartridges, so the cost per page is higher than the tank printers above. The Instant Ink trial can soften that for a while, but it is a subscription you will need to manage or cancel.

Buy it if you want a feeder and duplex at the lowest hardware cost, and your printing is light to moderate. Skip it if you print heavily, where a tank model recovers the extra price quickly.
pros: Feeder and duplex at a low price
cons: Cartridge ink costs more per page
products.idealFor: Light-to-moderate printers who want a feeder and duplex cheaply.

products.name: Canon MegaTank G3270 All-in-One Wireless Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The lowest entry price among the ink-tank picks, with no feeder or fax.
products.description:
Canon's MegaTank G3270 is a refillable-tank all-in-one with wireless printing, scan and copy, and a home-use design. It costs $100 to $200 and has a lower entry price than the other ink-tank picks.

It ranks fifth because it is the most basic of the tank group. The MegaTank system gives you the same economy of bottled ink, but without the feeder of the ET-4800 or the bundled ink of the HP Smart Tank. That makes it a simple pick for a budget-conscious buyer who wants low running costs and no extras.

Buy it if you want tank economics at the lowest entry price. Skip it if you need to scan paper stacks or want faxing.
pros: Lowest entry price for a tank
products.idealFor: Budget-minded buyers who want tank economics.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact entry printer for light home use, if you accept cartridge costs.
products.description:
The HP DeskJet 4355 is a compact color all-in-one that prints, scans and copies wirelessly, with a 3-month Instant Ink trial and AI-capable printing features. It is in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It ranks last because it is the plainest and the most ink-hungry option. The low price is an advantage when printing is occasional, since there is no big upfront cost. The cartridges, however, are small, and a household that prints regularly will pay far more over time than for a tank printer.

Buy it if you print a few pages a month and need a printer at the lowest price. Skip it if printing is a regular task.
products.idealFor: Occasional printing on a tight budget.

methodology.title: Running cost
methodology.description: We compared refillable ink-tank systems with cartridge inkjets, because the cost of ink over two years usually outweighs the purchase price.

methodology.title: Document handling
methodology.description: Automatic document feeders and duplex printing were scored on how much manual work they save in an office or home setting.

methodology.title: Connectivity
methodology.description: Wireless, 2.4GHz limits and Ethernet were checked, since a printer that is hard to connect becomes a daily irritation.

methodology.title: Footprint and design
methodology.description: Compact bodies and tank layouts were weighed against desk space in a typical home office.

methodology.title: Value inside the budget
methodology.description: Each model was set against the $50 to $100 and $100 to $200 price buckets, with a laser that exceeds the budget excluded.

whatMatters.factor: Cost per page, not price tag
whatMatters.detail: A cheap printer with expensive cartridges can cost several times its price in ink within a year or two. Tank printers invert that arithmetic with higher entry prices and cheap bottles. Estimate your monthly pages, then compare the two-year total.

Cartridges are cheap to buy and costly to refill, tanks are the reverse, and subscription plans like Instant Ink trade a monthly fee for ink delivery. Check the listing for words such as refillable, cartridge-free or MegaTank.

A feeder scans a stack in one pass, and duplex prints both sides automatically. They save time in home offices but add cost and size. Check the listing for the exact phrases automatic document feeder and automatic duplex.
Some printers connect only on the 2.4GHz band, and a router with a merged network can make setup confusing. Ethernet avoids the issue. Look for a stated band and a wired port on the listing.
Ink-tank printers hold their tanks in or beside the body, and some are wider than a bookshelf is deep. Measure your shelf or desk before buying, and leave room above for lid and tray clearance.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Small Home Office Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A feeder if you scan paperwork, duplex to save paper, and a running cost you can live with. A wired port helps if Wi-Fi is unreliable.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Epson ET-4800 for scanning-heavy work, or the HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e if you want a feeder and duplex at a lower price.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print every week and want to cut ink costs, or you need a feeder. The Epson EcoTank models and HP Smart Tank 5101 pay back the difference.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print occasionally and only need a basic scanner. The HP DeskJet 4355 will do.

faq.q: Is an ink tank printer worth it for light use?
faq.a: Usually not. If you print a handful of pages a month, a cheap cartridge printer costs less overall. Tanks pay off with regular printing, since the savings come from the low cost per page.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a cheap printer?
faq.a: Ignoring the ink. A low-priced printer with expensive cartridges costs more in the long run. Compare the two-year cost, not the purchase price.

faq.q: Is the Epson ET-2800 better than the HP Smart Tank 5101?
faq.a: They are close. The HP includes two years of ink and is smaller, while the Epson has no Wi-Fi band limit. Choose the HP if the included ink matters, and the Epson if your router uses a merged network.

faq.q: How do I fill the ink tanks?
faq.a: Open the tank cover, match the bottle color to the tank, and pour until the bottle empties or the tank is full. The bottles are keyed to avoid mixing colors. Wipe any drops with a paper towel.
It can for steady printers, since you pay a monthly fee for a set page count. If you print little, the fee can exceed the cost of cartridges. Cancel before the trial ends if it does not suit you.

faq.q: Why does my printer say the ink is low when it isn't?
faq.a: Printers estimate ink level by counting drops and pages, and the estimate can be off. If prints still look good, keep going. For tank printers, check the visible tank level.

finalTake: The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the best printer under $200 for most buyers, since refillable ink keeps the cost per page low. The HP Smart Tank 5101 is the better pick if included ink and a smaller body matter, and the Epson ET-4800 suits home offices that scan. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is the cheap way to get a feeder and duplex, and the DeskJet 4355 is only for occasional printing.
